title: Reuse scalable Boolean entailment for finite-domain CSP search and uniqueness
independentExamples: A three-house nonce puzzle with two renamed domains, equality, fixed-position, and direct-left constraints
The same finite-domain puzzle after entity and value renaming plus clue reordering
A contrast puzzle with a necessary ordering clue removed, producing more than one satisfying assignment
inputTypes: typed equality, position, non-position, order, adjacency, and exact-distance constraints
outputTypes: uniqueness certificate from an unsatisfiable blocked-assignment search
preconditions: Every domain contains exactly one value per position and has the declared house cardinality.
Every clue is parsed into one allowlisted typed constraint and retains its source-to-constraint correspondence.
The finite-domain encoding contains exactly-one constraints for values and positions.
The unchanged scalable Boolean method uses report-only inconsistency semantics.
invariants: A success requires a complete assignment that a separate direct constraint interpreter accepts.
A success requires the same constraint problem plus a blocking clause for the returned assignment to be independently certified unsatisfiable.
A non-unique, malformed, inconsistent, or resource-limited case never becomes a successful puzzle.
The generic Boolean core does not receive source identity, record identity, expected answers, puzzle vocabulary, or private labels.
Source and solver resource bounds never remove a retained row or reduce the declared denominator.
uncertaintySemantics: Parser failure, resource exhaustion, inconsistent parsed constraints, and non-uniqueness remain distinct non-success statuses. None is guessed or mapped to a private reference solution.
proofBehavior: The first generic SAT search yields a complete Boolean model, which is decoded and checked directly against every typed clue. A second search adds the negation of the complete chosen assignment; only an independently replayed unsatisfiability certificate establishes uniqueness.

resourceBounds.inherited: The frozen scalable Boolean method bounds semantic atoms, CNF variables, clauses, and DPLL search nodes per puzzle.
resourceBounds.streaming: The official source is streamed one JSONL record at a time and has no total-file-size acceptance cap.
resourceBounds.denominator: A per-puzzle resource limit is reported in aggregate and retains the puzzle in the tested denominator.

kbMigration: None. Source-specific surface aliases and reference cues stay inside the ZebraLogic adapter. No KB, runtime route, capability descriptor, engine module, or generic reasoning module changes.
decision: Reuse accepted. The existing generic Boolean solver is sufficient; only the source adapter, CSP projection, direct verifier, lifecycle controls, and receipts are added.
